hero.lead: An island nation of 9.4 million in the Caribbean, with farmland across six tenths of its land, where Cuba is not a member of the IMF or the World Bank and the capital on record is aid from partner governments, a UN food plan and climate grants.

capital.heading: Ten lines of aid and climate grants on record.

record.text: WFP Cuba country strategic plan, total cost to WFP from 1 July 2026 to 31 December 2030, approved by the WFP Executive Board in June 2026, for about 5 million people
Green Climate Fund financing for Cuba: two projects under implementation, with UNDP and FAO; readiness support of $7.0 million (read 23 November 2026)
EU humanitarian aid released on 23 July 2026, after a Caribbean regional allocation of €4 million, mainly for Cuba, in early 2026 and €2 million in April 2026

register.name: EU humanitarian aid for the Cuban population
register.detail: Released 23 July 2026 · grant through humanitarian partners on the ground · adds to €4 million in early 2026 and €2 million in April 2026
register.note: Medicines, maternal care, food and nutrition, water systems and renewable energy
register.text: The European Union released an additional €10 million in humanitarian aid for the most vulnerable people in Cuba, amid fuel shortages and the energy crisis. It finances medicines, primary and maternal healthcare, emergency food assistance and nutrition treatment for children and mothers, the rehabilitation of water systems and renewable energy solutions. It reaches four of the seven standards: health, food, water and energy.

register.name: Canada, new assistance to help Cubans
register.detail: Announced 17 April 2026 · C$5 million to PAHO · the rest to WFP
register.note: Essential health services and medicines; food assistance and logistics
register.text: Canada announced an additional $5.5 million (Canadian dollars) in international assistance for Cuba. The Pan American Health Organization receives $5 million to improve the availability of and access to essential health services, critical medicines and medical supplies; the World Food Programme receives the rest for food assistance and the logistics and fuel of the humanitarian response. It serves health and food.

register.name: EU humanitarian aid, logistics for relief
register.detail: Released 1 April 2026 · grant through humanitarian partners · logistics support
register.note: Relief amid disruptions to the distribution of food and drinking water
register.text: The European Union released an additional €2 million in humanitarian aid for Cuba, for logistics support to the partners delivering urgent relief to the most vulnerable. It responds to the energy crisis and to disruptions in the distribution of food and drinking water. It serves food and water.

register.name: Canada, food and nutrition for vulnerable Cubans
register.detail: Announced 25 February 2026 · accelerated funding released immediately · through WFP and UNICEF
register.text: Canada accelerated $8 million (Canadian dollars) of funding, released immediately, to scale up food and nutrition for vulnerable Cubans. It is delivered through the World Food Programme and UNICEF. Canada had provided over $3 million in humanitarian assistance after Hurricane Melissa in October 2025.

register.name: United States, humanitarian supplies through the Catholic Church
register.detail: Announced 5 February 2026 · delivered by the Catholic Church and Caritas · mainly in eastern Cuba
register.note: Food and solar lamps; reported by the Associated Press
register.text: The United States Department of State announced an additional $6 million in aid for Cuba, mainly for people in the eastern region, to be delivered by the Catholic Church and Caritas. The supplies include rice, beans, pasta, canned tuna and solar lamps. It follows $3 million of disaster relief for Cubans affected by Hurricane Melissa, and serves food and energy.

register.name: WFP Cuba country strategic plan 2026–2030
register.detail: Approved by the WFP Executive Board, June 2026 · 1 July 2026 to 31 December 2030 · about 5 million people
register.note: Total cost to WFP over the plan
register.text: The World Food Programme’s plan for Cuba to the end of 2030, approved by its Executive Board in June 2026, with a total cost to WFP of USD 116,425,668. It funds emergency food assistance and preparedness for shocks, nutrition for vulnerable groups through social protection, local food systems linked to school meals and other institutional markets, and supply chains for emergency responders. It aims to reach about 5 million people and serves food and livelihood, the two standards no survey yet measures in Cuba.

register.name: Mi Costa: coastal resilience through ecosystem-based adaptation (GCF FP157)
register.detail: Approved 19 March 2021 (B.28) · effective 13 September 2021 to 13 September 2029 · 83% disbursed · UNDP
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant of USD 23,927,294 for coastal resilience in Cuba, implemented by UNDP, with USD 20.4 million of co-financing. It restores mangroves, seagrass beds and coral reefs, the natural defences of the coastal communities where over 1.3 million vulnerable people live. Approved in 2021 and under implementation to 2029, it protects homes and so serves shelter.

register.name: IRES-Cuba: climate resilience of rural households and communities (GCF FP126)
register.detail: Approved March 2020 · seven years · FAO · GCF $38.2M and Government of Cuba $81.7M
register.note: GCF share of a project of about $119 million
register.text: A Green Climate Fund contribution of $38.2 million, with $81.7 million of co-financing from the Government of Cuba, for a seven-year project implemented by FAO. It introduces agroforestry on 35,000 hectares and improves the infiltration and retention of water in soils, for 240,000 people, including 52,000 family farmers. Approved in 2020 and still under implementation, it serves food and livelihood.

register.name: Japan, renewable energy for Cuban hospitals
register.detail: Announced 5 May 2026 · donation of the Government of Japan · implemented by UNDP over two years
register.note: Solar panels, power conditioners and storage batteries for hospitals in several provinces
register.text: A donation of $6.5 million from the Government of Japan, implemented by UNDP, to equip hospitals in several provinces of Cuba with solar generation: panels, power conditioners and storage batteries. It gives hospitals their own power during cuts, and serves health and energy, the two standards furthest from reach in Cuba.

register.name: China, aid for electrical equipment and urgent needs
register.detail: Approved by President Xi Jinping, confirmed 21 January 2026 · form not stated · with 60,000 tonnes of rice donated
register.note: Reported by Bloomberg Línea; no Chinese or Cuban government page opened
register.text: China approved US$80 million of aid for Cuba for the purchase of electrical equipment and other urgent needs, as its ambassador confirmed to the President of Cuba. China also donated 60,000 tonnes of rice, of which 30,000 had been delivered by January 2026, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Cuba. It serves energy and food.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.
items.alt: Tobacco fields and a thatched drying barn below limestone hills in the Viñales valley, Cuba

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: Tropical forest on steep mountain ridges above a clear river, eastern Cuba

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, end of 2025
items.text: 15% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A cobbled street of pastel colonial facades in Old Havana in morning light, with a classic car, Cuba

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.
items.alt: Green plains of sugar cane and royal palms below the Escambray mountains, central Cuba

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: A blue reservoir between forested hills with royal palms and a waterfall, central Cuba

items.name: Finca Marta
items.text: An eight-hectare agroecological family farm outside Havana that uses renewable energy and recycled water, receives visitors for farm-to-table meals and organises a network of about one hundred farms.

items.name: Artecorte
items.text: A community project in Old Havana, founded by a barber in 1999, that runs a free hairdressing school for young people, most of them out of work or study, in an alley it revived that now hosts more than 20 small local businesses.

coverage.gap_text: Of the basic list of medicines is not available to Cubans.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: No FAO food insecurity survey is published for Cuba. WFP reports that the state ration covered only 46% of recommended daily energy in 2023

guarantees.name: Water
guarantees.note: On 3 November 2026, 2,681,770 Cubans, 28.4% of the population, had their piped water cut (INRH). 95.2% have basic water (WHO/UNICEF, 2024)

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: Safely managed sanitation; 11% of city dwellers live in slums

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: At the evening peak on 10 November 2026 the grid could serve 970 of 2,900 MW of demand; the day before, supply was cut for all 24 hours. 96% cook with clean fuels (2024)

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 89.2% of young people complete lower secondary school

guarantees.name: Health
guarantees.note: Only 30% of the basic list of medicines is available (President of Cuba, August 2026). WHO service coverage index: 86 (2023)

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: No poverty survey is published for Cuba. WFP reports that a household needed ten to eleven times the minimum monthly wage to buy the food it needs (2023)
